newsitem.title: USA: Summit to acquire Collective Bancorp for $867 million.
newsitem.headline: Summit to acquire Collective Bancorp for $867 million.

text.p: Summit Bancorp, the leading operator of savings and loans in New Jersey, will acquire rival Collective Bancorp Inc. for $867 million in stock, the two companies said Friday.
Summit, which has 350 branches in New Jersey and eastern Pennsylvania, will add 82 branches in 15 New Jersey counties with the acquisition.
"The acquisition of Collective further secures Summit's number one market share position in New Jersey, especially in the growing shore markets," Summit Chairman T. Joseph Semrod said.
"The acquisition of Collective will afford Summit a strategic position in South Jersey that the company already enjoys in the northern and central regions of the state," Semrod added.
Collective shareholders will receive 0.895 share of Summit for each share of Collective in a tax-free swap, the companies said.
Based on the closing price of Summit common stock Thursday, the transaction has a value of $42.51 per Collective share, or a total of about $867 million, they said.
Summit closed Friday at $47.625 on the New York Stock Exchange and Collective closed at $42 on the Nasdaq market.
The merger, already approved by the boards of both companies, is expected to be completed by the third quarter, subject to regulatory and Collective shareholder approval, they said.
Summit said it will incur a one-time after-tax restructuring charge of about $33 million in connection with the acquisition.
Summit, based in Princeton, N.J., and has $23 billion in assets and $18 billion in deposits. Collective, a thrift holding company based in Egg Harbour City, N.J., has $5.5 billion in assets.
